In the past this was possible due to the same startpart, materials, checkprofiles. With Platon there will be a new startpart on DTAG site, new checkprofiles, new methodology in assigning material. Different positions in PLATON and NX in assemblies with nx assembly constraints
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug 📍 Location in the Process House (describe, in which part of the process the incident occurs - use Link to navigate) 05 Execute Design and Documentation: POSITIONING: Manage geometrical positioning 👉 For incident reproduction: Which action was taken? (Detailed step-by-step description, what you did) I opened an assembly with several parts in Central Test environment. The components of the assembly were positioned in NX before, by using assembly contstraints. I changed the relative transformation of the parts in PLATON and sent the assembly to NX, afterwards. 🚩 What was your expected result? I expected to be able to see the transformation out of PLATON inside my NX Session. 🐞 What was the actual result? (Please, insert screenshots/pictures/logfiles etc. as it is very helpful for us) The NX assembly constraints were still active and the transformations from PLATON were ignored. In NX an information messages shows up. 🚧 What are the consequences of the incident? Usually it is not recommended to use assembly constraints in NX. But there are use cases when it makes sense to work with them. Furthermore it happens that users create assembly constraints by mistake (e.g. automatic fix constraint creation when adding first component to an assembly). It is not possible to check the existence of assembly constraints from PLATON side. So the users may edit transformations in PLATON in such cases without knowing about the blocking assembly constraints in NX. The consequence is inconsistency between NX and PLATON. Because in PLATON the values of the transformation will be used and visualized in the 3D viewer, while NX will show the positioning given by the assembly constraints. My recommendation is to deactivate the present assembly constraints when the assembly is sent to NX. This is the current behaviour in Smaragd, as well. Default Platon Incident Template v. 4 from 20.09.2024 .

bug_title: Predecessor and/or successor of an element in Platon is not comprehensible
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug 📍 Location in the Process House (describe, in which part of the process the incident occurs - use Link to navigate) Product Engineering 👉 For incident reproduction: Which action was taken? (Detailed step-by-step description, what you did) In Palton, I created revision 0004 from a Part/Assembly Design revision with revision 0001 using the "Revision" command. Please see Image_01 in the attachments. 🚩 What was your expected result? Creating the revision 0004 in Platon worked perfectly! I then wanted to display the previous version of revision 0004, or I wanted to display the subsequent revision of revision 0001. Unfortunately, that wasn't possible. Please see Image_02 in the attachments. 🐞 What was the actual result? (Please, insert screenshots/pictures/logfiles etc. as it is very helpful for us) Unfortunately, it's not possible to display the predecessors and/or successors of an element in Platon. I'm thinking of the function in Smaragd where, by right-clicking on, for example, an item number, it was possible to determine the predecessor or successor. 🚧 What are the consequences of the incident? Knowing the history of a component is essential in vehicle development! Without being able to display for an element such as a part number which version of the part number it originated from or which versions originated from it, i.e., predecessors and successors, the history of a component cannot be traced. The ability to identify successors and predecessors, and thus determine the history of a component, is essential in a PDM system like Platon! Otherwise, serious errors in component statuses and significant time expenditures due to research activities are to be expected. Default Platon Incident Template v. 4 from 20.09.2024 .

bug_title: User can gain access to data, to which he should have no access via SendTo,PLATON Download, ...
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug This incident is not specific to one single use case but describes a general solution issue, that needs to be fixed. General description: Background: In PLATON we will have "mixed structures" - a structure where parts of the structure are assigned to different projects (some times even to secure or military projects). Example: Image a military Unimog -there are 90 % of the parts "normal parts that are assigned to e.g. "MBS series project A" because we have civil versions of that Unimog and we have a military version of it, but also 5% that are newly develop and part of a secure project (MBS Secure) and 5 %of the parts, like a camouflage head light, that are part of a military project (MBS Military). Issue description: If i am now a user who has access to the "MBS series project A", but NO access to (MBS Secure), or (MBS Military), than i can not see these parts in PLATON, but I can select the top node and use this top node to define a PLATON SendTo or SWAN object for extracting the data. As the extraction of these data is handled by a "super user - that has access to ALL projects" (like DC proxy) on the dispatcher, the complete structure including parts from (MBS Military) & (MBS Secure) will be exported and the user has access to these data, even so that he is not a member of the projects: (MBS Secure) & (MBS Military). Therefore the following PLATON (export) functionality need to be checked: •PLATON SendTo (file data + meta data) •PLATON Download (file data + meta data) •Send-Data with SWAN - SWAX: (file data + meta data) •PLATON Report (meta data only) •Rest API (meta data only ?) •BCS Snapshots (same solution used as in Download) •Creation of simplified jt or DMU envelop •... ? (if further functionality is affected to be evaluated) Expected Outcome: The requirement that needs to be fulfilled is: No matter what functionality a User is using in PLATON, he should never get more data out of the system, as he is allowed to see in the system. So where ever there is a asynchronous job performed on the dispatcher, or an Rest API is used, the technical user must reference to the access rights of the real user who has triggered that asynchronous job / the rest API, and all children of any selected top node must be checked, if user has access or not - not only the top node . All the functionalities must be able to handle Secure projects or military projects - restricting the functionality, so that it is not handling Secure projects or military projects is not an acceptable solution. 🚧 What are the consequences of the incident? User has access to data that he should not have - PLATON is not compliant with DTAG data security standards - especially critialc as 100% data load will be available soon in PLATON. This Incident affects at least a dozen BuSc. Default Platon Incident Template v. 4 from 20.09.2024 .

bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug 📍 Location in the Process House (describe, in which part of the process the incident occurs - use Link to navigate) n/a 👉 For incident reproduction: Which action was taken? (Detailed step-by-step description, what you did) To compare or display different component groups or other parts in one session it is currently required to create a "Workset" in which you can do that. It always creates an object in PLATON which can't get deleted or removed afterwards. Over time it will fill up the system with several such Worksets and potentially create capacity issues, not to mention the additional steps to create it in the first place. To do so you need to search for your desired object and open that one in PLATON to be able to create a Workset. It would be beneficial if there would be an option to send a search result object directly into an new to establish "temporary Workset" in which a designer can do all his activities he needs to do and after closing that "Temporary Workset" it gets purged or if PLATON gets closed it also gets purged right away. bug_title: Flaky behavior - Component Appears Checked-Out in NX but Not in AWC
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Summary : Component Z51785801 shows as checked out in Siemens NX by a user (Marcus Klug), but appears as not checked out in Active Workspace Client (AWC), even when viewed by the same user. This causes editing functions (e.g., add/delete child) to be greyed out and inaccessible to others (by me - FARRKHA). Steps to Reproduce : Open AWC with a user account (e.g., Marcus Klug). Search for and open component Z51785801. Observe that the component appears not checked out in AWC UI. Open the same component Z51785801 in NX using the same user login (Marcus Klug). Observe that in NX, the component is shown as checked out. As another user (e.g., Fareed Khan), attempt to perform actions like Add Child or Delete Child on component Z51785801 in AWC. Notice that these actions are greyed out despite the component showing as available for edit. Expected Behavior : If a part is checked out in NX, the checkout status should be synchronized and visible in AWC, regardless of where it's viewed from. bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Problem Summary : When a Geometry Revision is copied and pasted within the same assembly (A6635011257), the Rel. Count (Integer) to maintain referential integrity and ensure downstream systems and NX Add-ons function correctly. Actual Behavior : Multiple geometries share the same Rel. Count value, as shown. This violates assumptions in: NX Add-ons Downstream systems relying on uniqueness Business & Technical Impact : NX Add-ons malfunction or return incorrect results due to duplicated Rel. Count. Downstream PLM and BOM systems may break or misinterpret the structure. Model integrity is compromised, especially when changes are propagated.

bug_title: UGMASTER not Persistent after NX Save
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Bug to Platon Incident Incident Summary: Opening a Part / Assembly in NX when no UGMASTER exists causes NX to create a transient UGMASTER. After the user executes Save, this transient dataset is not written back to Teamcenter, leaving the item with no persistent UGMASTER. Steps to Reproduce: In PLATON, locate an Item Revision without a UGMASTER. e.g. A9603250944 Check Out the part using the ProductStructure Actions. Open in NX. NX generates a transient UGMASTER. File -> Save in NX; close the session. Refresh the item in PLATON → UGMASTER still absent. Required Resolution: Implement/restore post-save logic so that any transient UGMASTER is converted to a persistent UGMASTER dataset. bug_title: Non-CAD Attachment Shown as Component Thumbnail in LPS
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Bug to Platon Incident Problem Statement: When a user attaches an image in Primary -> Non-CAD attachments of an LPS component, AWC replaces the component’s normal thumbnail (JT preview / default icon) with that Non-CAD image. Non-CAD files must not drive the visual thumbnail for the component. Expected Result: The thumbnail in the structure tree and header should display only: The highest-priority graphic dataset (JT, PDF, etc.) or The default type icon when no preview dataset exists. Files added under Primary -> Non-CAD attachments must never override the thumbnail. Actual Result: After attaching a .png in Primary -> Non-CAD, the image instantly appears as the component thumbnail in AWC. Refreshing the session keeps the incorrect thumbnail. Steps to Reproduce: In AWC, open any LPS Object without a custom image thumbnail. e.g. Z51785801 Navigate to Attachments -> Files. Impact: Misleads users—thumbnail no longer represents actual geometry. Causes confusion in visual BOM reviews and release workflows. Inconsistent behavior vs. PLM thumbnail rules (only CAD/JT or preview dataset should apply). Upload an image file (e.g., sample.png). Observe the component card and the structure tree thumbnail. Observed: The uploaded image becomes the thumbnail. Expected: Thumbnail remains default JT preview or icon. bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Bug to Platon Incident Problem Statement Executing an advanced search in PLATON displays all historical revisions of each Search object. Instead of showing just the latest revision and providing older revisions in the revision history panel. This floods the results list, slows response time, and confuses users who expect a single hit per item. Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Problem Statement Executing an advanced search in PLATON displays all historical revisions of each Search object. Instead of showing just the latest revision and providing older revisions in the revision history panel. This floods the results list, slows response time, and confuses users who expect a single hit per item. Expected Result Search results should return one result per Object (the latest released or working revision). Earlier revisions should remain accessible via the Revision History Actual Result Search returns every revision for each matching item. Users must scroll large result sets and manually pick the newest revision. Steps to Reproduce From the PLATON Home screen, click the Advanced Search tile. In the drop-down (upper-left of the Advanced Search panel), select "02_DT_Component_Revision". In the Part Number field, type a value that has multiple revisions—for example Z52522092 Click on Search This returns multiple revisions of the same Object Type

bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Bug to Platon Incident 👉 Steps to reproduce Search and open a Part Assembly, Arragement or FlexPart with Geometry e.g. HKS9625202022 RMC to Geometry HKS9625202022_1 * 1 -> Revise -> Revise leads to an error RMC to Background -> Refresh and change to "History" (there is a version 5 for the Geometry) Open Version 5 of the Geometry and change to "Where Used" Go back to HKS9625202022 RMC -> Revise -> Revise leads to a new Version for the Part which links to the old version of the Geometry The old geometry needs to be replaced. This may cause multiple issues due to cross-links, and data could be lost in downstream processes 🚩 Expected result The Parent Item is also revised after Geometry Revise. 🐞 Actual result Revise leads to a new Version for the Part which links to the old version of the Geometry. Default Bug Template v. 2.0 from 10.04.2024. bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Description: It is currently possible to attach the same Part or Assembly with different revisions under the same Flexible Part. This violates the data integrity rules for Flexible Parts and can lead to inconsistencies in downstream processes like BOM validation, export, or release workflows. Steps to Reproduce : Open a Flexible Part (e.g. A0004286501_FP159) in Teamcenter. Add a Part or Assembly (e.g. A4375000408) twice under the Flexible Part. Revise only one of the instances of A4375000408. Observe that the same Part now exists under the Flexible Part with two different revisions. Expected Behavior : The system should prevent adding multiple revisions of the same Part / Assembly under a single Flexible Part. Once a revision is added, any attempt to add another revision of the same Part number should be blocked with an appropriate error or warning message. Actual Behavior: The system allows the same Part number with different revisions to coexist under the same Flexible Part without any warning or validation error. Screenshot / Evidence :

UGMASTER generation is only possible by running the "DT-Create derived UGMASTER from JT" workflow manually.

bug_title: Flexible parts displayed as original parts inside flexible part revisions
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug See attached .ppt file for screenshots Summary When viewing flexible part revisions, flexible parts are visible under 'Attachments -> Original Parts' the original part should appear. In the following screenshot, the first flexible part revision (e.g. A9408301715_FPA01, Rev 0001) shows: the original part A9408301715 (Rev 0001) and another flexible part (A9408301715_FPA02, Rev 0002) This violates the rule: Flexible parts should not be shown as original parts. bug_title: Flaky behavior - Component Appears Checked-Out in NX but Not in AWC
bug_description: 📄 Solution Request Context Change Description: Flaky behavior - Component Appears Checked-Out in NX but Not in AWC Reason for Change: Component Z51785801 shows as checked out in Siemens NX by a user (Marcus Klug), but appears as not checked out in Active Workspace Client (AWC), even when viewed by the same user. This causes editing functions (e.g., add/delete child) to be greyed out and inaccessible to others (by me - FARRKHA). Summary : Component Z51785801 shows as checked out in Siemens NX by a user (Marcus Klug), but appears as not checked out in Active Workspace Client (AWC), even when viewed by the same user. This causes editing functions (e.g., add/delete child) to be greyed out and inaccessible to others (by me - FARRKHA). Steps to Reproduce : Open AWC with a user account (e.g., Marcus Klug). Search for and open component Z51785801. Observe that the component appears not checked out in AWC UI. Open the same component Z51785801 in NX using the same user login (Marcus Klug). Observe that in NX, the component is shown as checked out. As another user (e.g., Fareed Khan), attempt to perform actions like Add Child or Delete Child on component Z51785801 in AWC. Notice that these actions are greyed out despite the component showing as available for edit. Expected Behavior : If a part is checked out in NX, the checkout status should be synchronized and visible in AWC, regardless of where it's viewed from. The user who has checked out the part should see it marked as such in both NX and AWC. Other users should see the part as checked out and be prevented from editing, but with a proper indication. Impact if Not Implemented: Users are confused about the checkout status. Actions on the component are inaccessible or blocked without a clear reason. Which BuSc are affected? bug_title: Bus structure has different Bom elements
Effectivity date shifts and wrong revision is selected when filtering by milestone date
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Description When a Part / Assembly Design Revision is attached to a Milestone, the part’s Effectivity does not exactly match the Milestone’s Valid From Date. Example milestone: 2844926 – VSO_Test, Milestone Valid From Date = 2025-07-01. Attached part: A9534200129. After attachment, the part shows Effectivity = 'MSAssigned 2025/06/30 22:00:28 to UP (TTX-EI)' (see screenshot), i.e., one day earlier than the milestone date. Environment / Context Structure context: Z54356539 with child A9534200129. Client timezone: CET/CEST (Germany). Steps to Reproduce Create a Milestone (e.g., 2844926 – VSO_Test) with Milestone Valid From Date = 2025/07/01. Attach A9534200129 (Part / Assembly Design Revision) to the milestone. Open the assembly Z54356539. Inspect A9534200129 in the right-side “Overview” pane → Effectivity. Change the Date filter in the structure header to: 2025/07/02 2025/07/01 and note which revision is shown each time. Actual Results Date shift in Effectivity: The part shows Effectivity start = 2025/06/30 22:00:28, i.e., 2 hours before midnight on 2025/07/01, instead of exactly 2025/07/01 00:00. Revision selection inconsistency: - With Date = 2025/07/02, the structure shows revision 0001 of A9534200129 (the one just attached to the milestone) and its effectivity 2025/06/30 22:00:28 → UP. - With Date = 2025/07/01, the structure does not show revision 0001; instead it shows an older revision 0001.002 (released 2023/03/04 with effectivity 2023/06/01 12:00 → UP). Expected Results The part’s Effectivity start should be exactly equal to the milestone’s Valid From Date (2025/07/01 00:00, in a time zone-safe representation). When filtering the structure by a date (as-of view), the system should select the newest revision whose effectivity start ≤ filter date (ascending-term-chain semantics). Therefore, both 2025/07/01 and 2025/07/02 filters should select revision 0001, not fall back to older 0001.002. Logical Analysis / Likely Root-Cause The 22:00:28 timestamp strongly suggests a UTC vs. local time conversion issue: Milestone is date-only (2025-07-01) and likely written as 2025-07-01T00:00 local. When persisted or rendered, it appears to be converted to UTC, yielding 2025-06-30T22:00:28Z (≈ local midnight minus ~2h), which is then displayed back to users.

bug_title: Milestone “At Most” allows creating a new Revision between existing released effectivities (and even on the same date), breaking the ascending date chain
bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Impact: Causes wrong revision to be found/used in production filters Summary Users can create a Milestone and assign it to a newer Revision (0001) of a part with a “Valid from” date that falls between the released effectivity dates of earlier revisions (e.g., between 2024-06-01 of 0001.002 and 2025-09-01 of 0002.001 ). This breaks the ascending effectivity chain and leads to incorrect filter results : searching for a released part valid after the first effectivity returns the milestone-assigned 0001 instead of the actually released 0001.002 . A second edge case exists where the milestone date equals a released revision’s effectivity (e.g., 2025-09-01 ): the system allows assigning a different revision with the same date, creating two competing states on one DMU appointment . Steps to Reproduce Open part e.g. A0134309164 and review released revisions and effectivity dates (as above). Create a Milestone with Valid from = 01.03.2025 12:00:00 (between 2024-06-01 and 2025-09-01). Assign revision 0001 to this milestone. bug_title: Fields from ECO not inherited by Part attached to it
bug_description: **Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug** The following attributes are not inherited from an ECO to a part: Type of Release ![image.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/706ba318-70b5-4f6f-a734-a14ea601014e?fileName=image.png) When a part is attached to an ECO, the attached part should inherit the following attributes in the following release scenarios: Screenshots from SMARAGD have also been attached at the end: | Platon Attribute | SMARAGD Attribute | SMARAGD Technical Name | Standard (with Drawing and/or 3D) | kZ-Siehe (with reference) | kZ Release (no Draw; lubricants etc) | | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | | Type of Release | Freigabeart | j0IsUVKZ | j0IsUVKZ = '' | j0IsUVKZ = j0DSTKZS | j0IsUVKZ = j0KZ | | Drawing Number | Hinweiszeichnungnummer | j0HNumber | j0HNumber = '' | j0HNumber = 'Drawing Number' | j0HNumber = '' | PLATON currently accepts any values for 'Drawing Number' when defining the release method: ![image.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/8f1a6433-eb65-4a90-acd2-bf317b592c3a?fileName=image.png) In case of kZ-Siehe, PLATON should check if the drawing number has a valid format. Note: The system does not check if the drawing is actually present. If the Drawing Number isn't valid, then the following error message should be displayed: ``` The ECO–part relationship cannot be created/changed. The value for *“Drawing number”* does not have a valid format. Please select a valid value for *“Drawing number”* according to the current guideline. Examples of valid formats: **A2208870201, HAA1234567890**. ``` For reference, see screenshot below: SMARAGD throws the following error when a drawing number is entered with an incorrect format: ![Pasted image 20250904144158.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/56d2e99c-61be-4335-9740-936f889225a9?fileName=Pasted%20image%2020250904144158.png) Subsequently, when a part is removed from an ECO, the following values should be cleared out on the part 1. Drawing Number 2. Effectivity 3. Change Number 4. ZGS 5. Type of Release Milestone should also be removed. Screenshots from SMARAGD for reference: ![2025-09-04 14_03_32-Common Validation_Testing of Greenlist _ Daimler Truck _ FARRKHA@tbdir.net _ Mic.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/41fc26f3-8ee9-45dd-b490-e7951a9b6d8b?fileName=2025-09-04%2014_03_32-Common%20Validation_Testing%20of%20Greenlist%20_%20Daimler%20Truck%20_%20FARRKHA@tbdir.net%20_%20Mic.png) ![2025-09-04 14_10_39-Common Validation_Testing of Greenlist _ Daimler Truck _ FARRKHA@tbdir.net _ Mic.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/cbe59547-6f69-4526-b3a9-10813840b08a?fileName=2025-09-04%2014_10_39-Common%20Validation_Testing%20of%20Greenlist%20_%20Daimler%20Truck%20_%20FARRKHA@tbdir.net%20_%20Mic.png) ![2025-09-04 14_14_38-Common Validation_Testing of Greenlist _ Daimler Truck _ FARRKHA@tbdir.net _ Mic.png](https://dev.azure.com/CORPTB/b064d2c3-fc8a-4fe1-a7c5-6f1164367a12/_apis/wit/attachments/2f69ace7-f4d8-4c92-ba6c-faecc42c497b?fileName=2025-09-04%2014_14_38-Common%20Validation_Testing%20of%20Greenlist%20_%20Daimler%20Truck%20_%20FARRKHA@tbdir.net%20_%20Mic.png)

bug_description: Copied from Repro Steps when changed from Platon Incident to Bug Environment / Preconditions System: Teamcenter AWC (PLATON) – pre04 Milestone: TSO_2025.03.01 , Valid from: 2025-03-01 Part: A0134309164 Revisions present: 0001 (MSAssigned via Milestone), 0001.002 (Released 2024-06-01 12:00:00), 0002.001 (Released 2025-09-01 12:00:00) Repro Steps Create Milestone TSO_2025.03.01 with Valid from = 2025/03/01 . Attach A0134309164 / 0001 to this Milestone. Status becomes MSAssigned . Open the structure view and set filters: Milestone: TSO_2025.03.01 Date: 2025/03/01 → Observe shown revision. Expected Result On the milestone day ( 2025/03/01 ), with Milestone=TSO_2025.03.01 , the system must resolve to revision 0001 (the revision attached to that Milestone). A user should be able to create a milestone but NOT assign 'Valid from' Date to it. i.e. Allowed: User should be able to create a 'Milestone Exact' Not Allowed: User should NOT be able to create a 'Milestone At Most' There should NOT be any time conversion here . bug_description: Call GET /sma4u/compliance?partnumber= &version= Inspect the DSDZ array objects in the response Observe that only p4d_eff_from, p4d_eff_till, and p4d_sma_project_name are returned Note: p4d_feature_number, all j0 atomic fields, and composed display names are missing Expected Behavior Per the original User Story #184968, the API specification states: “Response should have all the p4d_* attributes along with basic OOTB attributes” Each compliance entry must include the following additional fields. The PLATON attribute p4d_feature_number (on object type P4DComplianceRel , Integer) is confirmed to exist in the data model. CR1: Missing p4d_feature_number The p4d_feature_number attribute (Integer, on P4DComplianceRel ) must be included in each compliance entry. This field is a sequential running number that uniquely identifies each compliance feature within the scope of a TB . When a TB contains multiple ZBs, each ZB may carry its own set of DS/DZ compliance entries. The p4d_feature_number provides a unique, TB-scoped integer index across all ZBs — e.g., ZB1 might have features 1, 2, 3 and ZB2 might have features 4, 5. This running number is the only way to ensure a consistent, non-overlapping feature numbering across all ZBs aggregated under one TB. Without p4d_feature_number , consuming systems have no TB-scoped identifier to uniquely address individual compliance features across ZB boundaries, breaking traceability and preventing reliable data correlation at TB level. CR2: Missing German and English display names In the former SMARAGD system, each DZ-Feature carries atomic attributes that are composed into standardized display names. These names are written to PREEvision CustomerFeature attributes and displayed to engineers. German (name_de): [ ] fuer gemaess English (name_en): [ ] for according to Without pre-composed names, downstream systems must parse the composite object_name string, losing structural information. CR3: Missing j0 atomic fields The following fields exist on the PLATON DZ-Feature object ( P4DDZForm ) and must be included in the compliance response: Field Type Description Example p4d_feature_number Integer Sequential running number, unique per TB (on P4DComplianceRel) 3 j0FeatureId Integer Unique DZ-Feature ID 7835 j0FeatureName String German feature name Pruefbericht oder Bauteilgenehmigung fuer Kabelbrandpruefung / Anhang 10 j0FeatureNameEngl String English feature name Test Report or Component Approval relating to Cable resistance to flame / Annex 10 j0SubjectArea String German subject area Brennbarkeit j0SubjectAreaEngl String English subject area Flammability j0Market String Market/region ECE j0Regulation String Regulatory reference UNECE-R 118/03 j0AdditionalInfo String Certificate number (ZK-Nr) BUS0135, BVE K name_de String Composed German display name Pruefbericht ... [Brennbarkeit] fuer ECE gemaess UNECE-R 118/03 name_en String Composed English display name Test Report ... [Flammability] for ECE according to UNECE-R 118/03 Expected fields per compliance feature (subset of full API response) Note: The JSON below does not represent the full /sma4u/compliance API response. It shows the expected attribute set for a single compliance feature entry within the DSDZ array. The full API response wraps this in the broader TB-to-ZB relation structure (TB metadata, table_objects containing one or more ZB entries, each with their own compliance array). The fields listed here are the missing attributes that must be added to each individual compliance feature object within that existing structure. { "object_name": "Pruefbericht oder Bauteilgenehmigung fuer Kabelbrandpruefung / Anhang 10,ECE,7835", "object_type": "DZ-Feature", "p4d_feature_number": 3, "p4d_eff_from": "2019-10-01T00:00:00Z", "p4d_eff_till": "9999-01-01T00:00:00Z", "p4d_sma_project_name": "", "j0FeatureId": 7835, "j0FeatureName": "Pruefbericht oder Bauteilgenehmigung fuer Kabelbrandpruefung / Anhang 10", "j0FeatureNameEngl": "Test Report or Component Approval relating to Cable resistance to flame / Annex 10", "j0SubjectArea": "Brennbarkeit", "j0SubjectAreaEngl": "Flammability", "j0Market": "ECE", "j0Regulation": "UNECE-R 118/03", "j0AdditionalInfo": "BUS0135, BVE K", "name_de": "Pruefbericht oder Bauteilgenehmigung fuer Kabelbrandpruefung / Anhang 10 [Brennbarkeit] fuer ECE gemaess UNECE-R 118/03", "name_en": "Test Report or Component Approval relating to Cable resistance to flame / Annex 10 [Flammability] for ECE according to UNECE-R 118/03" } Actual Behavior Only p4d_eff_from , p4d_eff_till , and p4d_sma_project_name are returned. All other p4d_* and j0 fields are missing. Impact p4d_feature_number: This is a sequential running number scoped to the TB — it uniquely indexes each compliance feature across all ZBs within a TB (e.g., ZB1: features 1,2,3; ZB2: features 4,5). Without it, there is no TB-scoped unique identifier for compliance features, making it impossible to consistently address and correlate features across ZB boundaries. j0 atomic fields: Without individual fields, consumers must parse the composite object_name string — losing 4 of 7 atomic fields and all English text. Display names (name_de / name_en): PREEvision writes these to CustomerFeature attributes displayed to engineers. Without pre-composed names, the display is incomplete. Without these fields, the only alternative is the deprecated SMARAGD API (end-of-life), which is not acceptable for production use.

bug_title: PLATON sma4u API: /items/files/query does not return P4DCirKit (KBL) datasets
bug_description: Problem The PLATON TruckAPI endpoint POST /platon_sma4u/v1/items/files/query does not return KBL files stored as P4DCirKit (Circuit Kit) datasets. This blocks any partner system using the TruckAPI from downloading KBL files programmatically for HKH parts. Background Per ADO #340329 (FM | Change mapping for Migration of kbl files as P4DCirKit, state: DOD), KBL files were intentionally re-mapped to the P4DCirKit dataset type during SMARAGD migration, based on file attributes RelativePath / WorkingRelativePath / j0OriginalFileName ending in .kbl. The TruckAPI was not updated to reflect this new dataset structure. Per ADO #414169 (SendToKBLViewer, state: New), KBL files must be identifiable via P4DCirKit alone (extension can be .xml or .kbl for legacy/migrated data, .kbl for PLATON native data). This is the authoritative identification path -- not the file extension. Detailed Evidence (production, part HKH666821T026) TC object model (from AWC browser session HAR analysis) P4DDesignRevision (HKH666821T026, UID: UZDzUvdgPFswlD) -> IMAN_specification -> UGMASTER (HKH666821T026.prt, UID: 0P31BGiyPFcXwC) -- returned by TruckAPI, no KBL here -> [not exposed via TruckAPI] -> P4DCirKit (HKH666821T026_0001.06, UID: SgzlQ3w6PFc5EA) -> ref_list -> ImanFile: HKH666821T026_0001_06.kbl (UID: EwHZpRYBPF8jdA) TruckAPI calls tested (all failed to return KBL) GET /gen/relations?p4d_part_number=HKH666821T026 -- returns only UGMASTER (.prt) and P4DDesignRevisionMaster; P4DCirKit not visible POST /items/files/query with relation_type: IMAN_specification, IMAN_Rendering, TC_Attaches, IMAN_reference, CMHasSolutionItem, IMAN_UG_altrep -- none return the KBL POST /items/files/query with derived_files=true -- returns only technologydata.xml (Collector, NX port data); not the KBL POST /items/files/query with dataset_uid=UGMASTER-UID and derived_files=true -- same result, no KBL How AWC frontend retrieves the KBL (for reference) AWC calls getDeclarativeStyleSheets for the P4DDesignRevision -> finds P4DCirKit tab with ref_list -> calls getFileReadTickets with ImanFile UID EwHZpRYBPF8jdA directly. This TC SOA path is not available via TruckAPI. Expected Behavior POST /items/files/query for an HKH part number must also traverse and return files attached via P4DCirKit datasets. The response entry should include original_file_name, original_file_ext, and a valid FMS download ticket -- consistent with what the AWC frontend already shows and with ADO #414169 requirements. Scope of Impact All HKH parts whose KBL was migrated from SMARAGD as P4DCirKit (per ADO #340329) are affected. This is not limited to PREEvision -- any partner system using /items/files/query to retrieve KBL files is impacted. Workaround None available via TruckAPI. Direct TC SOA session (browser SSO) is the only current path to retrieve the KBL, which is not feasible for automated/headless systems. Reported by Petzsche, Christian (028) -- PEER team, Daimler Buses. Contact via JIRA DBPREE-818.

Impact if Not Implemented ECO workflows for maturity‑only changes will continue to fail unnecessarily. Increased process delays , manual workarounds, and repeated support tickets. Risk of non‑compliance with change governance , as users may switch change types incorrectly. Higher operational effort and reduced efficiency for the users. Allow ECO workflow to proceed and pass validation for parts connected with Historic Tolerance , provided maturity is the only change. Validation rules should be applied only when the Type of Change includes technical or drawing updates (e.g., AE) . Proposed Mitigation Introduce a conditional validation check based on Type of Change . If AEoZ + maturity‑only , bypass rules related to tolerance modification. Maintain existing validation behavior for AE / technical change scenarios .
